$comment: Held-out evaluation labels (scripts/eval.py). knownPositives come from a code audit by an AI agent (Claude) that read only the project's source at the pinned revision: it did not run Midwrite and did not see its output. findings are classified afterwards, finding by finding, with the Phase 2 classes. No independent human review has been performed; an AI agent checking another AI agent's results is not independent human validation. Corrections go in `corrections` with a reason, never by editing a label to raise a score.

knownPositives.scope: unhandled half-written-state windows in server code; the audit was capped at 30 entries, highest confidence first, so the list is a sample when the project has more

findings.by: AI agent (Claude), finding-by-finding source review, separate from the auditor; did not see knownPositives

knownPositives.consequence: If the activity dies after the provider accepted the message, Temporal retries the activity and sends again; nothing dedups by messageId before sending.
Dedup reads the events written at line 413, so a crash between sending and submitBatch makes the retried activity re-send the whole batch.
Messages are delivered without delivery records; a client retry (random messageId) re-sends to every user.

knownPositives.secondEffect: clickhouseClient().insert(...) at line 161, then pruneIndex 171 and backfillIndex 180
knownPositives.consequence: Postgres records the index while ClickHouse is not configured/pruned/backfilled; a retry sees the same type and skips both, leaving the index incomplete.

knownPositives.secondEffect: chCommand(DELETE FROM user_property_index_config) at line 226, then pruneIndex at 232
knownPositives.consequence: The Postgres row is gone while the ClickHouse config keeps indexing; a retry returns early because the row is missing, so it is never cleaned up.

knownPositives.firstEffect: db().transaction(...) bumping the segment version at line 275 (update at 311)
knownPositives.secondEffect: submitBatch(...) ManualSegmentUpdate events per chunk at line 359
knownPositives.consequence: The new version commits before membership events are written, so a failure mid-chunk leaves the segment empty or partial after the capped retries.
The event is stored but event-entry journeys never start; nothing re-triggers them.

knownPositives.secondEffect: triggerEventEntryJourneys(...) per track event at line 143
knownPositives.consequence: Batch events persist while some event-entry journeys never start.

knownPositives.secondEffect: insertProcessedComputedProperties(...) ClickHouse processed marker at line 3746
knownPositives.consequence: A crash before the processed marker makes the retry re-signal and re-run completed journeys that can run multiple times.

knownPositives.firstEffect: chCommand(INSERT INTO user_events_v2 SELECT ... cold storage) at line 96
knownPositives.consequence: Events are restored but cold rows remain; a re-run duplicates events.

knownPositives.secondEffect: chCommand(DELETE FROM user_events_v2 / internal_events) at line 59
knownPositives.consequence: Events are copied but not removed; a re-run duplicates them in cold storage.
The workspace is Active and recomputed while its events are still in cold storage.
The reactivated workspace runs with its history still in cold storage.
The global scheduler skips the workspace while no per-workspace compute workflow exists, so computed properties stop updating.

knownPositives.secondEffect: db().transaction(...) updating the journey node variant type at line 286
knownPositives.consequence: The template's channel changes while the journey node keeps the old channel type.
Uploaded users' traits are written but their manual segment membership is never updated.

findings.notes: segmentsController.ts:440-448 publishes identify events (random messageIds) before updateManualSegmentUsers; no compensation or retry, so traits are ingested but membership is unchanged.
persistFiles (apps/files.ts:18-28,36-72) writes under a deterministic messageId key before submitTrack (apps.ts:65); only an overwritable orphan blob can remain.
Same upload-then-reference pattern: persistFiles (apps.ts:101) uses a messageId-keyed path before submitBatch (:118).
Bootstrap code: terminateComputePropertiesWorkflow is best-effort (lifecycle.ts:130-141) and the later inserts are idempotent upserts, so re-running converges.
bootstrapWorkspace (bootstrap.ts:499-506) seeds demo events behind a flag and startGlobalCron swallows failures: re-runnable bootstrap code.
triggerBroadcast (broadcasts.ts:363-393) uses a deterministic workflowId, tolerates already-started, and the activity sets Triggered itself (performBroadcast.ts:59-62).
processRowsInner (computePropertiesIncremental.ts:3683-3746) is deliberately at-least-once with deterministic per-user workflowIds and versioned updates.
removeFeatures (features.ts:160-190) is called only from the admin CLI; the delete is idempotent and start errors are swallowed, so re-running converges.
journeys.ts:1183-1194 needs status===Running && journey.status===Paused, but journey is the row returned after the transaction set the status (1084-1094, 1141): the branch is unreachable.
recordNodeProcessed runs in a Temporal activity; onConflictDoNothing on a unique index (recordNodeProcessed.ts:50) and a deterministic uuidv5 messageId (:56) make retries converge.
sendMessageWithSender is a retry-aware Temporal activity (activities.ts:270-300) and submitTrack reuses the deterministic messageId (:385); a possible duplicate send is the accepted cost.
storeEmailForViewInBrowser (messaging.ts:998-1014) is explicitly best-effort and writes a messageId-keyed object.
getMultiTenantRequestContext (requestContext.ts:270-345) re-checks and upserts a missing member/account on every request.
appendToManualSegment is a Temporal activity (maximumAttempts 5) with deterministic uuidv5 messageIds (activities.ts:220-223): retries converge.
replaceManualSegment is a retried activity whose version derives from the workflow's fixed now (manualSegmentWorkflow.ts:103-111) and submitBatch uses deterministic messageIds.
Same activity-retry convergence: the transaction at activities.ts:275 is idempotent for a given now and the recompute at :386 is re-run by Temporal.
submitBatch (activities.ts:359) uses deterministic messageIds and enqueueRecompute (:386) runs inside a retried Temporal activity.
updateUserSubscriptions (subscriptionGroups.ts:780-786) writes ClickHouse assignments and the source-of-truth events concurrently without compensation; a recompute can revert the unsubscribe.
deleteUsers (users.ts:1525-1557) runs ClickHouse deletes and two Postgres deletes in Promise.all without a transaction or retry: partly deleted user data.
deleteAllUsers (users.ts:1594-1611): the same Promise.all pattern workspace-wide.

handleOauthCallback (dashboard/src/lib/oauth.ts:258-323) commits tokens and the integration before startHubspotIntegrationWorkflow (its only caller); a failure leaves the integration enabled without a sync workflow.

The account-link insert (requestContext.ts:337-344, onConflictDoNothing) and the domain auto-join role inserts (88-97, onConflictDoNothing) are lazy get-or-create steps that run on every authenticated request. findAndCreateRoles recomputes the missing domain roles each time (81-83), so an account row without its role is fixed on the user's next request. Until then the user just looks not-onboarded, which is harmless by design. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 returned-builder change.)

Window is real: storeEmailForViewInBrowser (messaging.ts:999, S3 putObject in viewInBrowser.ts) runs before sendMailSmtp -> transport.sendMail (smtp.ts:56), and a failed send leaves a stored body. But the store is an auxiliary view-in-browser copy: its own failure is only logged as a warning and sending continues (messaging.ts:1004-1012), the blob is keyed by messageId (overwritten on retry) and is reachable only via the hashed link inside the email, so an unsent email leaves an unreachable, harmless orphan object. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

Same pattern on the SendGrid branch: storeEmailForViewInBrowser (messaging.ts:999) then sendMailSendgrid -> sendgridMail.send (sendgrid.ts:55, which is awaited via ResultAsync by the caller). The leftover is a view-in-browser blob keyed by emails/{workspaceId}/{messageId}/body.html, treated as non-critical (store failure only warns, messaging.ts:1004-1012), idempotent on retry and unreachable without the email's hashed link, so the partial state is harmless by design. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

Same pattern on the Resend branch: storeEmailForViewInBrowser (messaging.ts:999) then sendMailResend -> resend.emails.send (resend.ts:33). The window exists, but the blob is a best-effort side copy for view-in-browser (failure logged as warn and ignored, messaging.ts:1004-1012), overwritten on retry under the same messageId key and only reachable via a link in the sent email, so an orphan after a failed send is harmless. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

Audited dittofeed-KP16: upsertMessageTemplate commits its own transaction before the controller transaction changes the matching journey-node channel. The two are not atomic. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Re-runnable bootstrap: upsertWorkspace uses stable workspace identity and addFeatures/terminateComputePropertiesWorkflow performs best-effort workflow reconfiguration. Same bootstrap policy as existing 7323fd6e3fa25fbe. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Bootstrap seeds a workspace and its get-or-create write key in separate steps. Both are checked/upserted on subsequent bootstrap calls; partial setup is intentionally re-runnable. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Bootstrap obtains a write key and upserts the default subscription group separately. This is the re-runnable, idempotent bootstrap sequence, not a one-shot business transaction. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Default email and SMS subscription groups use deterministic uuidv5 IDs and upserts. A partially completed bootstrap can be re-run to finish the other default group. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

The audited KP02 delivery/submitBatch window exists in a retried Temporal activity, with deterministic per-recipient event message IDs. Retain the same accepted at-least-once delivery interpretation as the existing KP01 finding ece472399ebf7efb; this is hazard detection, not confirmation that provider delivery is deduplicated. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

The computed-property processor independently dispatches journey and integration assignments in an at-least-once processing pipeline. Existing processRowsInner finding 641d7d73ce314294 documents the accepted deterministic workflow/versioned-update retry model. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Administrative resetComputePropertiesWorkflows intentionally processes workspaces independently. terminateComputePropertiesWorkflow catches/logs termination errors, and the bulk operation does not promise atomic completion across workspaces. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Administrative reset across distinct workspaces, some terminated and some reset according to their status. The operation is intentionally per-workspace and best-effort rather than one atomic cross-workspace change. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

The first operation is a HubSpot OAuth token exchange. Source alone does not establish whether receiving a new token invalidates an older credential or creates consistency-relevant provider state. Do not treat POST alone as proof of a business mutation. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

The proposed path combines a successful database token upsert with an AxiosError/BAD_REFRESH_TOKEN-only catch branch. This appears to mix incompatible success and failure paths, but confirming the exact exception provenance needs a stronger error/result model. Excluded from precision pending review. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

The code concurrently creates new HubSpot email records and updates existing ones in a retried integration activity. The source shows separate effects, but does not establish whether provider-side identity/reconciliation makes retry converge. No independent provider review performed. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Same unreachable restart branch as existing 29694cf677dd7e5d and removed KP04: UPDATE RETURNING provides the new status, so requested Running cannot coexist with returned journey.status Paused. Recognizing the wrapped database write exposes an additional MW1001 occurrence of this existing path-correlation limitation. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

A journey insert/update commits before enqueueRecompute for newly running manual-entry journeys. If enqueue fails after the commit, a retry can observe the already-running journey and not reproduce the transition flag. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Same provider-send/submitTrack window and at-least-once activity interpretation as ece472399ebf7efb. Tracing-wrapper coverage reports it at the enclosing specialized call as well; the auditor/labeler disagreement remains unresolved. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP03: the API waits for per-user delivery before submitBatch records the results. There is no shared atomic boundary; a client retry with generated message IDs can resend messages whose records were never persisted. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

getRequestContext now exposes the getMultiTenantRequestContext member/account get-or-create writes through its tracing wrapper. As documented for existing 985208f60c8a5189, each subsequent request checks and repairs missing member/account links. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

deleteSegment commits the PostgreSQL deletion before ClickHouse cleanup. Once the row is absent, retry returns early, so the remaining ClickHouse data is not cleaned by that retry. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

deleteUserProperty commits the PostgreSQL deletion before ClickHouse cleanup. A retry sees no deleted row and returns early, leaving stale ClickHouse state. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP05: the PostgreSQL property-index transaction commits before ClickHouse config insertion and backfill. Retrying with an unchanged type can skip the pending backfill. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

ClickHouse config is inserted before pruneIndex removes the previous type data. These external writes are not atomic; once PostgreSQL has the new type, retry may no longer select the old-type cleanup branch. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Old-type pruning and new-type backfill are separate ClickHouse commands after the PostgreSQL type update. A crash can leave the index pruned but not backfilled, and retry can skip the type-change branch. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP06: PostgreSQL deletion commits before ClickHouse config deletion. A retry finds no index and returns early without completing ClickHouse cleanup. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

ClickHouse configuration deletion and pruneIndex data deletion are separate commands. After PostgreSQL index deletion, a retry exits early and cannot finish a failed prune. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

deleteUsers performs ClickHouse deletions and PostgreSQL assignment/dependency deletions without a shared transaction or durable completion record. Partial deletion can survive a process crash. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

deleteAllUsers similarly deletes across ClickHouse and separate PostgreSQL statements without an atomic boundary; a crash can leave data present in only one store. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP12: coldStoreWorkspaceEvents copies events to cold storage before deleting the hot user events. Failure before deletion leaves duplicate copies and a re-run can insert them again. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Same audited KP12 cold-copy window before the separate internal_events deletion. The two hot-store deletions are independent commands. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP11: restoreWorkspaceEvents copies cold rows into the hot table before deleting the cold rows. A crash/re-run can duplicate restored events. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

tombstoneWorkspace commits the status/name change before moving its events to cold storage. A crash can leave the workspace tombstoned while its data has not been cold-stored. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP14: the reactivation transaction commits before restoreWorkspaceEvents; an active workspace can remain without its historical hot events. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

pauseWorkspace updates its PostgreSQL status before coldStoreWorkspaceEvents. The status change does not atomically move the events, so a crash can leave mixed lifecycle/data state. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

Audited dittofeed-KP13: resumeWorkspace marks the workspace Active before restoring cold events, without a shared atomic boundary. (2026-11-12 Codex AI source review after development fixes; not blind or independently human-validated.)

corrections.reason: Provider delivery followed by submitTrack/submitBatch is a pair of independent external effects, not an external effect followed by a modeled PostgreSQL commit. The event helpers call insertUserEvents, which publishes to Kafka or inserts into ClickHouse. Keep the evaluator strict about the diagnostic code; correct the audited pattern instead of accepting unrelated codes in the same function. No finding classification changed.
evidence: packages/backend-lib/src/apps/batch.ts:68-112: submitBatch calls submitBatchChunk, which calls insertUserEvents.
packages/backend-lib/src/userEvents.ts:90-145: insertUserEvents writes to Kafka or ClickHouse.
corpora/configs/dittofeed.json: submitTrack and submitBatch are message-publish external effects (configuration unchanged).

previous.firstEffect: db().transaction(...) committing status Paused->Running at line 988
previous.consequence: The journey is Running but the restart workflow never starts; a retried upsert sees Running and never restarts re-entry users.

corrections.reason: The audited crash window assumes restartUserJourneyWorkflow is reachable after changing Paused to Running. The UPDATE sets the requested status and returns the updated row. Outside the transaction journey is that updated row, so status === Running implies journey.status === Running, contradicting the restart guard journey.status === Paused. This is an unreachable restart branch, not an executed operation that a crash can interrupt. Remove this window from the recall denominator; keep finding 29694cf677dd7e5d false-positive. A possible application logic bug in the unreachable branch is outside this partial-write evaluation.
evidence: packages/backend-lib/src/journeys.ts:1083-1095: UPDATE sets status and uses RETURNING.
packages/backend-lib/src/journeys.ts:1122-1141: the transaction returns journey: updated; the outer scope destructures that journey.
packages/backend-lib/src/journeys.ts:1183-1198: restart requires requested status Running and updated journey.status Paused.
packages/backend-lib/src/db.ts:65-78: queryResult awaits the supplied query and wraps its result without replacing the returned row.
